title: Wagering
subtitle: Tote pools, ticket sales and pari-mutuel settlement
summary: Wagering runs the tote: pools per race and bet type (WIN, PLACE, SHOW, EXACTA, QUINELLA, TRIFECTA) with their takeout, idempotent ticket sales on five channels, automatic pool closing at the off, and settlement from the certified result with dividends, breakage, minus pools and refunds.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: In pari-mutuel betting the club does not take a position: all stakes go into a pool, the takeout percentage is the club's revenue, and the rest is shared by the winners as a dividend per 1.00 staked. Rounding down creates breakage, which also belongs to the club.
Pools close themselves within seconds of the race starting (a scheduled job polls Race Operations). A cancelled race voids its pools and refunds every ticket.
Each ticket sale carries an idempotency key, so a double click at a busy window sells one ticket, not two.

sections.title: Wagering database architecture · Visual ERD
sections.intro: A physical view of wagering: five domain tables and seven declared foreign keys. The diagram separates the tote data from external references to Race Operations and Enterprise Core.

sections.title: How a betting pool works — in everyday language
paragraphs: Imagine ten visitors each place a $10 WIN bet on a race. Their combined stakes make a $100 pool. At a hypothetical 15% takeout, the club retains $15 and $85 remains available for winning dividends before any other settlement adjustments. This is an illustration, not a claim about configured rates.

Unlike fixed-odds betting, the payout is calculated from everyone’s combined stakes and the winning stakes, rather than a price locked when the bet was placed. The winning result has to be certified before the payout is finalized.

A ticket is not merely a receipt: the database keeps the pool it belongs to, the wager amount, the exact selection or combination, a unique ticket number and an idempotency_key. That final field helps stop an accidental double click or retry from creating two purchases.

sections.title: Database protections versus application responsibilities
items: Database enforces: one pool per race and bet type; unique ticket numbers and idempotency keys; positive stake; takeout percentage from 0 to 100; one settlement per pool.
Database enforces: settlement arithmetic gross_handle = takeout_amount + net_pool and non-negative settlement amounts.
Service must enforce: pool-open rules, correct bet selections, valid race-entry combinations, certified results, and race-off handling. Foreign keys alone cannot do those jobs.
Service must enforce: payout formulas, rounding/breakage, refunds, minus pools, and consistency between ticket state and ledger events. The uploaded DDL does not encode these algorithms.
Architecture lesson: accounting events should link operational settlement to General Ledger without losing the source transaction or duplicating financial postings.

terms.definition: One per race and bet type: OPEN, SUSPENDED, CLOSED, SETTLED or VOID, with a takeout percentage.
Selections, stake, channel (ON_COURSE, TELEPHONE, ONLINE, MOBILE, KIOSK). ISSUED → WON / LOST → PAID, or REFUNDED.
The club's share of the gross pool, per bet type (TAKEOUT_WIN ...).
Payout per 1.00 staked on a winning combination, after takeout and breakage.
When guaranteed minimum dividends exceed the net pool, the club makes up the difference (MINUS_POOL).

sections.title: Design decisions
items: Settlement refuses to run until the result is OFFICIAL in Race Operations.
Settlements and declared dividends are immutable (database guards).
Pool liability sits on GL 2210 until settlement, dividends payable on 2200 until paid by Prizes.
